editorial.note: Line etching, drypoint, and metal punch printed in blue-green, on a yellow-green ground, colored with brush; second state of two. Drawings and Prints.

Presumably made during Savery’s trip in the Tyrol, this drawing was once owned by Rembrandt. In the description of his estate, mention is made of a large book containing drawings that Savery made in the Tyrol.
In his biography of Roelant Savery, Joachim von Sandrart recounts that Emperor Rudolf II commissioned the artist to go to the Tyrol to record its ‘remarkable wonders of nature’.
